back: A type the programmer defines to represent the data of a problem more accurately than the built-in types.
A type whose values are a list of named constants, e.g. TYPE TDay = (Mon, Tue, Wed); the order allows comparison.
A type whose value is the memory address of another value; dereferencing follows the address to the value.
A composite type with fields of different types under one name: TYPE ... DECLARE field : type ... ENDTYPE.
A composite type: an unordered collection with no duplicates; operations are membership, union, intersection and difference.
Non-composite: enumerated, pointer. Composite: record, set, class (object).
Enum for enumerated types, dataclass or class for a record, set for a set.
Limit the allowed values, group related data, make code readable and safer.
An array holds items of one type; a record groups fields of different types; an array of records holds many items.
